topic: Natural Language Processing: Transformers, Attention, and Tokenization

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: A quantitative hedge fund deploys a sentiment-extraction engine to analyze financial disclosures (SEC Form 10-K filings) containing dense numerical tables, ticker symbols (e.g., '$BRK.A'), and accounting terms (e.g., 'EBITDA-adjusted'). The production model uses a standard BERT-base checkpoint equipped with a general-domain WordPiece tokenizer (30,522 vocabulary size). During real-time processing, inference latency surges by 320%, and the downstream classifier fails to capture critical financial entities because specialized terms are split into 6 to 10 fragmented subwords, routinely breaching the strict 512-token input limit.
questions.question: Which architectural adaptation strategy directly resolves this high subword fertility rate and input truncation without requiring full, compute-prohibitive pre-training from scratch?
options: A) Switch to pure character-level tokenization to eliminate out-of-vocabulary conditions and maintain fixed-length sequence buffers.

B) Apply domain-adaptive vocabulary expansion by appending prioritized domain tokens to the vocabulary, initializing their embeddings via weighted averages of constituent subwords, and executing continual masked language modeling.
C) Increase the maximum sequence length parameter to 2048 by interpolating sinusoidal positional encodings without altering tokenizer vocabulary.
D) Replace WordPiece with Byte-Level Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) while keeping the original general-domain vocabulary intact to compress input sequences.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Apply domain-adaptive vocabulary expansion by appending prioritized domain tokens to the vocabulary, initializing their embeddings via weighted averages of constituent subwords, and executing continual masked language modeling.
questions.explanation: High subword fertility (number of tokens generated per word) occurs when a tokenizer trained on general corpora (e.g., Wikipedia) encounters out-of-domain technical terminology. This inflates sequence lengths, triggering context truncation and attention dispersion. Expanding the tokenizer vocabulary with domain-specific terms lowers fertility and preserves semantic cohesion. Initializing the new token embeddings using average representations of their existing subword decompositions prevents random gradient shocks, and continual pre-training (domain adaptation) aligns them within the latent semantic space. Character-level tokenization (A) exponentially worsens sequence length. Positional interpolation (C) does not fix excessive fragmentation and increases self-attention compute quadratically. Switching to BPE without vocabulary modification (D) does not alter domain-specific subword fertility.

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: A legal tech enterprise is processing long-context contracts averaging 16,384 tokens per document using an open-source Transformer model. During distributed evaluation across dual NVIDIA A100 (40GB) GPUs, the forward pass persistently crashes with CUDA Out-Of-Memory (OOM) errors at the self-attention layer. Memory profiling indicates that while the model parameters occupy merely 14 GB of VRAM, the intermediate attention score matrix allocation fails when calculating softmax((Q K^T) / sqrt(d_k)).
questions.question: Which attention optimization technique eliminates this memory bottleneck by computing mathematically exact self-attention without materializing the intermediate N x N attention matrix in GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM)?
options: A) Linformer Attention, which projects the sequence dimension of Keys and Values onto a fixed low-rank dimension k using learned projection matrices.
B) FlashAttention, which leverages SRAM tiling and online softmax rescaling to compute attention blocks iteratively without storing the quadratic intermediate matrix in HBM.
C) Reformer Attention, which utilizes Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) to approximate nearest-neighbor query-key pairs in O(N log N) space.
D) Sliding Window Attention with dilation, which limits the receptive field of each query to a fixed local window of tokens.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) FlashAttention, which leverages SRAM tiling and online softmax rescaling to compute attention blocks iteratively without storing the quadratic intermediate matrix in HBM.
questions.explanation: Standard self-attention materializes an N x N matrix (where N = 16,384 tokens), requiring storage of (16384^2 * 4 bytes * heads * layers) in GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM), which causes immediate OOM. FlashAttention restructures the computation to be IO-aware: it loads blocks of Queries, Keys, and Values from HBM into fast on-chip SRAM, computes local attention, uses an online softmax formulation to rescale intermediate results dynamically, and writes only the final output back to HBM. This achieves exact standard attention (non-approximated) while reducing memory complexity from O(N^2) to O(N) relative to HBM access. Linformer (A), Reformer (C), and Sliding Window (D) are approximate attention mechanisms that alter the underlying mathematical formulation and reduce semantic context.

questions.scenario: Real-world Industrial Problem Statement: An autonomous customer support platform serves thousands of concurrent dialogue sessions using a 70-billion-parameter auto-regressive Transformer model. During token-by-token generation (decoding phase), GPU compute utilization (TFLOPS) hovers below 18%, yet inference throughput throttles severely. Profiling indicates that GPU High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) bandwidth is 100% saturated due to repeatedly fetching the Key-Value (KV) cache across 64 attention heads for each generated token under high batch concurrency.
questions.question: Which structural modification to the multi-head attention mechanism addresses this memory-bandwidth bottleneck in the KV cache while maintaining competitive model expressiveness?
options: A) Multi-Query Attention (MQA), collapsing all Query, Key, and Value projections into a single shared scalar projection head.
B) Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), where Query heads are partitioned into groups that share a single Key and Value head per group.
C) Cross-Attention decoupling, where Key and Value projections are evaluated only once during prompt encoding and frozen throughout decoding.
D) Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) compression, which quantizes the phase shift angles of query-key inner products to reduce cache bit-depth.
questions.correct_answer_text: B) Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), where Query heads are partitioned into groups that share a single Key and Value head per group.
questions.explanation: During autoregressive decoding, generation is memory-bandwidth bound (arithmetic intensity is low) because the KV cache must be transferred from HBM to compute units for every single token step. In standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA), each query head has its own Key and Value head. Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) groups query heads together to share a single Key-Value head pair (e.g., 8 KV heads shared across 64 Query heads). This slashes the memory footprint and memory bandwidth read overhead of the KV cache by an 8x factor, dramatically lifting memory-bound throughput constraints while preserving significantly more modeling capacity and quality than Multi-Query Attention (MQA, which forces only 1 single KV head for all queries). Option C violates auto-regressive context updates, and Option D mischaracterizes RoPE.
